title: Bayern Munich’s Manuel Neuer set for three-week thigh injury layoff, to miss Dortmund game
content:
Manuel Neuer is set to miss three weeks with a thigh injury, a setback that will see him miss Bayern Munich’s match against Borussia Dortmund this month.

Neuer, 39, was withdrawn at half-time of Bayern’s 3-0 victory at Werder Bremen on Saturday, and is now set to miss next week’s game against Frankfurt and the February 28 clash against Dortmund.

Vincent Kompany’s side are six points clear of Dortmund at the top of the Bundesliga.

Back-up goalkeeper Jonas Urbig, who replaced Neuer in Bremen, is set to deputise in the absence of the veteran. Neuer has made 589 first-team appearances for Bayern since joining from Schalke in 2011, while Urbig joined the Bavarian club from FC Koln in 2024.

Earlier this week, Neuer ruled out the possibility of coming out of retirement to play for Germany at the 2026 World Cup.

There will be two consequences of this. The first, obviously, will be an extended run for Urbig in the first team, which will include the game against Dortmund at the end of the month.

Get through that unscathed and Bayern will be on the road to defending their title. Their position is advantageous, but for Urbig it will be highly pressurised; is he really up to succeeding Neuer? Nobody really knows yet.

The second impact will be a discussion about Neuer; his goalkeeping remains at a really high standard, but his body seems increasingly fragile. His contract is due to expire at the end of the season, so a decision about that will have to be made soon.

He suffered three injuries last season, each of which cost him match time, and this will be his second lower-leg issue of 2025-26.

His literal absence should not be too costly, but what about the break in continuity ahead of the Champions League knockout rounds? That’s less than ideal and yet, like last year, it’s become a feature of Bayern seasons.
